verses.1:1: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking down the Amalekites, that David remained in Ziklag two days.
verses.1:2: And it came to pass on the third day, behold, a man came from the camp, from Saul, with his garments torn and earth upon his head. And when he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
verses.1:3: And David said to him, "From where are you coming?" And he replied to him, "I have escaped out of the camp of Israel."
verses.1:4: And David said to him, "How did the matter turn out? Tell me, please." And he replied, "The people have fled from the battle, and moreover, many of the people have fallen and died; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead as well."
verses.1:5: Then David said to the young man who told him, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"
verses.1:6: And the young man who told him said, "As I happened by chance to be upon Mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and behold, the chariots and the horsemen pressed hard after him.
verses.1:7: And when he looked behind him, he saw me and called to me. And I answered, 'Here I am.'
verses.1:8: And he said to me, 'Who are you?' And I said to him, 'I am an Amalekite.'
verses.1:9: Then he said to me, 'Stand over me, please, and slay me, for anguish has seized me, yet my life is still wholly in me.'
verses.1:10: So I stood over him and slew him, because I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was upon his head and the armlet that was upon his arm, and have brought them here to my lord."
verses.1:11: Then David took hold of his own garments and tore them, and likewise did all the men who were with him.
verses.1:12: And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
verses.1:13: Then David said to the young man who had told him, "Where are you from?" And he answered, "I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite."
verses.1:14: And David said to him, "How is it that you were not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?"
verses.1:15: Then David called one of the young men and said, "Draw near and strike him down!" And he struck him so that he died.
verses.1:16: And David said to him, "Your blood be upon your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I have slain the LORD's anointed.'"
verses.1:17: Then David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
verses.1:18: and he commanded them to teach the children of Judah the Bow; behold, it is written in the Book of Jashar:
verses.1:19: "The splendor of Israel lies slain upon your high places! How the mighty have fallen!
verses.1:20: Do not tell it in Gath, do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon—lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
verses.1:21: O mountains of Gilboa, let there be neither dew nor rain upon you, nor fields of offerings! For there the shield of the mighty was defiled—the shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
verses.1:22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
verses.1:23: Saul and Jonathan were beloved and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not parted; they were swifter than eagles, they were mightier than lions.
verses.1:24: O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with finery, who set ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
verses.1:25: How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan lies slain upon your high places!
verses.1:26: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; you have been exceedingly dear to me; your love to me was more wondrous than the love of women.
verses.1:27: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!"
verses.2:1: And it came to pass after this that David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go up to any of the cities of Judah?" And the LORD said to him, "Go up." And David said, "Where shall I go up?" And He said, "To Hebron."
verses.2:2: So David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.2:3: And David brought up his men who were with him, every man with his household; and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
verses.2:4: Then the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, "It was the men of Jabesh Gilead who buried Saul."
verses.2:5: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh Gilead, and said to them, "Blessed are you of the LORD, because you have shown this lovingkindness to your lord, to Saul, and have buried him.
verses.2:6: And now may the LORD show lovingkindness and truth to you; and I also will show you this goodness, because you have done this thing.
verses.2:7: Now therefore, let your hands be strengthened, and be men of valor; for your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has also anointed me king over them."
verses.2:8: But Abner the son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim;
verses.2:9: and he made him king over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel, over Ephraim, over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.2:10: Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David.
verses.2:11: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
verses.2:12: Now Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.2:13: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out and met them together by the pool of Gibeon. So they sat down, these on the one side of the pool, and those on the other side of the pool.
verses.2:14: Then Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men now arise and hold a contest before us." And Joab said, "Let them arise."
verses.2:15: So they arose and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
verses.2:16: And each one grasped his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent's side, so that they fell down together. Therefore that place was called Helkath Hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
verses.2:17: And the battle was exceedingly fierce on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before the servants of David.
verses.2:18: Now the three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. And Asahel was as swift of foot as one of the gazelles in the open field.
verses.2:19: And Asahel pursued Abner, and as he went he did not turn aside to the right hand or to the left from following Abner.
verses.2:20: Then Abner looked behind him and said, "Is it you, Asahel?" And he answered, "It is I."
verses.2:21: And Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and lay hold of one of the young men, and take his armor for yourself." Yet Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
verses.2:22: So Abner spoke yet again to Asahel, "Turn aside from following me! Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I lift up my face to Joab your brother?"
verses.2:23: However, he refused to turn aside. Therefore Abner struck him in the belly with the butt end of the spear, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there and died on the spot. And it came to pass that all who came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
verses.2:24: Joab and Abishai also pursued Abner. And the sun was going down when they came to the hill of Ammah, which lies before Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.2:25: Now the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together behind Abner and formed one band, and they stood upon the top of a hill.
verses.2:26: Then Abner called to Joab and said, "Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? How long then will it be before you tell the people to turn back from pursuing their brethren?"
verses.2:27: And Joab said, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, surely even in the morning the people would have withdrawn, every man from following his brother."
verses.2:28: So Joab blew the trumpet; and all the people stood still and did not pursue Israel any further, nor did they fight anymore.
verses.2:29: Then Abner and his men marched through the Arabah all that night; and they crossed over the Jordan, and marched through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
verses.2:30: And Joab returned from pursuing Abner; and when he had gathered all the people together, there were missing of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel.
verses.2:31: But the servants of David had struck down of Benjamin and of Abner's men, so that three hundred and sixty men died.
verses.2:32: Then they took up Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb, which was in Bethlehem. And Joab and his men marched all night, and the day dawned upon them at Hebron.
verses.3:1: Now the war was long between the house of Saul and the house of David; and David grew steadily stronger, while the house of Saul grew steadily weaker.
verses.3:2: And sons were born to David in Hebron: his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
verses.3:3: and his second, Chileab, by Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur;
verses.3:4: and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
verses.3:5: and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.3:6: Now it came to pass, while the war continued between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was strengthening his hold in the house of Saul.
verses.3:7: Now Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah; and he said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"
verses.3:8: Then Abner became exceedingly angry at the words of Ishbosheth, and said, "Am I a dog's head that belongs to Judah? This day I show lovingkindness to the house of Saul your father, to his brethren and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of David; yet today you charge me with an iniquity concerning this woman!
verses.3:9: May God do so to Abner, and more also, for just as the LORD has sworn to David, surely so I will do for him:
verses.3:10: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba."
verses.3:11: And he could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.
verses.3:12: Then Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, "Whose is the land?" and saying, "Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand shall be with you to bring all Israel over to you."
verses.3:13: And he said, "Good; I will make a covenant with you. Yet one thing I ask of you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see my face."
verses.3:14: So David sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Saul's son, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
verses.3:15: And Ishbosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel the son of Laish.
verses.3:16: Then her husband went along with her, weeping as he walked behind her as far as Bahurim. And Abner said to him, "Go, return!" And he returned.
verses.3:17: Now Abner had conferred with the elders of Israel, saying, "In time past you were seeking David to be king over you.
verses.3:18: Now therefore do it! For the LORD has spoken concerning David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
verses.3:19: And Abner also spoke in the hearing of Benjamin. Then Abner also went to speak in the hearing of David in Hebron all that was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of the whole house of Benjamin.
verses.3:20: So Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made a feast for Abner and for the men who were with him.
verses.3:21: Then Abner said to David, "I will arise and go, and gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may reign over all that your soul desires." So David sent Abner away, and he departed in peace.
verses.3:22: And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a raid and brought much spoil with them. But Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
verses.3:23: When Joab and all the army that was with him arrived, they told Joab, saying, "Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace."
verses.3:24: Then Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Behold, Abner came to you; why is it that you sent him away, and he is altogether gone?
verses.3:25: You know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing."
verses.3:26: And when Joab had gone out from David's presence, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah; yet David did not know it.
verses.3:27: Now when Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside inside the gate to speak with him privately, and there struck him in the belly so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
verses.3:28: And afterward, when David heard of it, he said, "I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner.
verses.3:29: Let it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house; and let there never be cut off from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or a leper, or one who holds a spindle, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread."
verses.3:30: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had put their brother Asahel to death at Gibeon in the battle.
verses.3:31: Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your garments, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner." And King David walked behind the bier.
verses.3:32: So they buried Abner in Hebron; and the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.
verses.3:33: And the king sang a lament over Abner and said, "Should Abner die as a fool dies?
verses.3:34: Your hands were not bound, nor were your feet put into bronze fetters; as a man falls before sons of iniquity, so you fell." And all the people wept over him once more.
verses.3:35: Then all the people came to urge David to eat bread while it was still day; but David swore, saying, "May God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down!"
verses.3:36: And all the people took note of it, and it was good in their eyes, as indeed everything the king did was good in the eyes of all the people.
verses.3:37: So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it had not come from the king to put Abner the son of Ner to death.
verses.3:38: Then the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?
verses.3:39: And I am weak today, though anointed king; and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too harsh for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his wickedness."
verses.4:1: When Saul's son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands grew feeble, and all Israel was dismayed.
verses.4:2: Now Saul's son had two men who were captains of raiding bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin—for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin,
verses.4:3: and the Beerothites had fled to Gittaim and have been sojourners there to this day.
verses.4:4: Now Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son who was crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the tidings of Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel; and his nurse took him up and fled. And it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
verses.4:5: Then the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, set out and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, while he was taking his noonday rest.
verses.4:6: And they came right into the midst of the house, as though to fetch wheat, and they struck him in the belly; and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
verses.4:7: For when they had entered the house, while he was lying on his bed in his bedchamber, they struck him and put him to death, and cut off his head; and they took his head and went by way of the Arabah all that night.
verses.4:8: And they brought the head of Ishbosheth to David at Hebron, and said to the king, "Behold, the head of Ishbosheth, the son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life! And the LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day upon Saul and upon his offspring."
verses.4:9: Then David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul from all adversity,
verses.4:10: when one told me, saying, 'Behold, Saul is dead,' and thought in his own eyes that he was a bearer of good tidings, I seized him and slew him in Ziklag—which was the reward I gave him for his tidings.
verses.4:11: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous man in his own house upon his bed? Therefore, shall I not now require his blood at your hand and purge you from the earth?"
verses.4:12: So David commanded the young men, and they slew them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the grave of Abner in Hebron.
verses.5:1: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and spoke, saying, "Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
verses.5:2: Furthermore, in times past, when Saul was king over us, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing them in; and the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall become ruler over Israel.'"
verses.5:3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.5:4: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
verses.5:5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.5:6: And the king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to David, saying, "You shall not enter here, for the blind and the lame will turn you away," thinking, "David will not enter here."
verses.5:7: Nevertheless, David captured the stronghold of Zion—that is, the City of David.
verses.5:8: Now David said on that day, "Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him reach by way of the water shaft even the lame and the blind, who are hated by David's soul." Therefore they say, "The blind and the lame shall not enter the house."
verses.5:9: Then David dwelt in the stronghold and called it the City of David. And David built all around from the Millo and inward.
verses.5:10: So David grew greater and greater, and the LORD God of hosts was with him.
verses.5:11: Then Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar timbers, carpenters, and stonemasons; and they built a house for David.
verses.5:12: And David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, and that He had exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.
verses.5:13: And David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.5:14: Now these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
verses.5:17: Now when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. And David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
verses.5:18: The Philistines came and spread themselves out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.5:19: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?" And the LORD said to David, "Go up, for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand."
verses.5:20: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David struck them down there; and he said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breakthrough of waters." Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
verses.5:21: And they abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.
verses.5:22: Then the Philistines came up once again and spread themselves out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.5:23: And when David inquired of the LORD, He said, "You shall not go up; circle around behind them, and come upon them in front of the balsam trees.
verses.5:24: And it shall be, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then you shall move decisively, for then the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines."
verses.5:25: So David did just as the LORD had commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines from Geba as far as the approach to Gezer.
verses.6:1: And David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.6:2: And David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name—the Name of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned above the cherubim.
verses.6:3: So they set the ark of God upon a new cart and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.
verses.6:4: They brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, accompanying the ark of God; and Ahio went before the ark.
verses.6:5: And David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all manner of instruments of cypress wood, and with lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals.
verses.6:6: And when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.
verses.6:7: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence; and he died there beside the ark of God.
verses.6:8: And David became angry because the LORD had broken out in a breach against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, to this day.
verses.6:9: And David feared the LORD that day, and he said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"
verses.6:10: So David was not willing to move the ark of the LORD with him into the City of David; instead, David turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.6:11: And the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
verses.6:12: Now it was told to King David, saying, "The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with gladness.
verses.6:13: And it came to pass, when those who bore the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, that he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
verses.6:14: Then David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
verses.6:15: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.
verses.6:16: Now as the ark of the LORD came into the City of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through a window and saw King David leaping and whirling before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
verses.6:17: So they brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. And David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
verses.6:18: And when David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
verses.6:19: Then he distributed among all the people, among the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, to each one a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins. So all the people departed, each to his own house.
verses.6:20: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How glorious was the king of Israel today, uncovering himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his servants, as one of the base fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!"
verses.6:21: So David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before the LORD.
verses.6:22: And I will be even more undignified than this, and will be humble in my own eyes. Yet by those maidservants of whom you have spoken, by them I shall be held in honor."
verses.6:23: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.
verses.7:1: Now it came about, when the king was dwelling in his house and the LORD had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,
verses.7:2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look now, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, yet the ark of God dwells within the curtain."
verses.7:3: And Nathan said to the king, "Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you."
verses.7:4: And it came to pass in that night that the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
verses.7:5: "Go and say to My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD: Shall you build for Me a house for My dwelling?
verses.7:6: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up the children of Israel from Egypt even to this day, but I have been walking about in a tent and in a tabernacle.
verses.7:7: In every place where I have walked among all the children of Israel, did I speak a word to any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built for Me a house of cedar?"'
verses.7:8: Now therefore, thus shall you say to My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over My people, over Israel.
verses.7:9: And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you; and I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great men who are on the earth.
verses.7:10: And I will appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more; nor shall the sons of wickedness afflict them any more, as at the first,
verses.7:11: even from the day that I commanded judges to be over My people Israel. Moreover, I will give you rest from all your enemies. And the LORD declares to you that the LORD will make a house for you.
verses.7:12: When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who shall come forth from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.7:13: He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
verses.7:14: I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to Me. When he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the sons of men.
verses.7:15: Yet My lovingkindness shall not depart from him, as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
verses.7:16: And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before you; your throne shall be established forever.'"
verses.7:17: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
verses.7:18: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said, "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me thus far?
verses.7:19: Yet even this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, and You have spoken also concerning the house of Your servant for a great while to come—and this is the law of man, O Lord GOD!
verses.7:20: And what more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.
verses.7:21: For the sake of Your word, and according to Your own heart, You have done all this greatness, to make it known to Your servant.
verses.7:22: Therefore You are great, O LORD God; for there is none like You, nor is there any God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.7:23: And who is like Your people, like Israel, the one nation on the earth whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people, and to make for Himself a name, and to do for you great and awesome deeds for Your land, before Your people whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
verses.7:24: For You have established for Yourself Your people Israel as Your very own people forever; and You, O LORD, have become their God.
verses.7:25: And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word which You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, and do as You have spoken.
verses.7:26: So let Your name be magnified forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel.' And let the house of Your servant David be established before You.
verses.7:27: For You, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed to the ear of Your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' Therefore Your servant has found it in his heart to pray this prayer to You.
verses.7:28: And now, O Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are truth, and You have spoken this goodness to Your servant.
verses.7:29: Now therefore, let it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You; for You, O Lord GOD, have spoken it, and with Your blessing let the house of Your servant be blessed forever."
verses.8:1: Now it came to pass after this that David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
verses.8:2: He also struck Moab, and he measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground; and he measured two lines to put to death and one full line to keep alive. So Moab became servants to David, bringing tribute.
verses.8:3: David also struck Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his dominion at the River Euphrates.
verses.8:4: And David captured from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David also hamstrung all the chariot horses, except that he reserved enough of them for one hundred chariots.
verses.8:5: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men among the Arameans.
verses.8:6: Then David placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became servants to David, bringing tribute. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.
verses.8:7: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.8:8: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a very great quantity of bronze.
verses.8:9: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,
verses.8:10: then Toi sent Joram his son to King David to inquire of his welfare and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him—for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi—and in his hand were vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze.
verses.8:11: These also King David dedicated to the LORD, along with the silver and the gold that he had dedicated from all the nations which he had subdued:
verses.8:12: from Aram, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, from Amalek, and from the spoil of Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.8:13: And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand of the Arameans in the Valley of Salt.
verses.8:14: He also placed garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he placed garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And the LORD preserved David wherever he went.
verses.8:15: So David reigned over all Israel, and David administered justice and righteousness to all his people.
verses.8:16: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder.
verses.8:17: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was scribe.
verses.8:18: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and the sons of David were priests.
verses.9:1: Now David said, "Is there still anyone who is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him lovingkindness for the sake of Jonathan?"
verses.9:2: Now the house of Saul had a servant whose name was Ziba. When they had called him to David, the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "Your servant."
verses.9:3: And the king said, "Is there not still someone of the house of Saul, to whom I may show the lovingkindness of God?" And Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan who is lame in his feet."
verses.9:4: So the king said to him, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
verses.9:5: Then King David sent and brought him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
verses.9:6: When Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell on his face and prostrated himself. And David said, "Mephibosheth." And he answered, "Behold, your servant!"
verses.9:7: Then David said to him, "Do not fear, for I will surely show you lovingkindness for the sake of Jonathan your father, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your grandfather; and you shall eat bread at my table continually."
verses.9:8: Then he bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should look upon such a dead dog as I?"
verses.9:9: And the king called Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son.
verses.9:10: You therefore, and your sons and your servants, shall till the land for him, and you shall bring in the produce, that your master's son may have bread to eat; yet Mephibosheth your master's son shall eat bread at my table continually." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.9:11: Then Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so shall your servant do." "And Mephibosheth," replied the king, "shall eat at my table as one of the sons of the king."
verses.9:12: Now Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Micha. And all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
verses.9:13: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the table of the king. And he was lame in both his feet.
verses.10:1: Now it came to pass after this that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:2: Then David said, "I will show lovingkindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, just as his father showed lovingkindness to me." So David sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father; and the servants of David came to the land of the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:3: And the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Is David honoring your father in your sight, because he has sent comforters to you? Has David not sent his servants to you in order to search out the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?"
verses.10:4: Therefore Hanun seized the servants of David, shaved off half of their beards, cut off their garments at the middle up to their buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.10:5: When they told David, he sent to meet them, for the men were exceedingly ashamed. And the king said, "Remain in Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return."
verses.10:6: Now when the sons of Ammon saw that they had become odious to David, the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-Rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and from the men of Tob twelve thousand men.
verses.10:7: When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the host of the mighty men.
verses.10:8: Then the sons of Ammon came out and drew up in battle array at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
verses.10:9: When Joab saw that the battle front was against him both before and behind, he chose from all the select men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.
verses.10:10: And the rest of the people he placed under the hand of Abishai his brother, and he arrayed them against the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:11: And he said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall come to my deliverance; but if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will go and deliver you.
verses.10:12: Be strong, and let us show ourselves valiant for our people and for the cities of our God; and may the LORD do what is good in His sight."
verses.10:13: So Joab and the people who were with him drew near to battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him.
verses.10:14: And when the sons of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled, they also fled before Abishai and entered into the city. Then Joab turned back from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
verses.10:15: When the Arameans saw that they had been routed before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
verses.10:16: And Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's host going before them.
verses.10:17: When it was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Arameans drew up in battle array against David and fought with him.
verses.10:18: Then the Arameans fled before Israel, and David slew of the Arameans the men of seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen; and he struck down Shobach the commander of their host, so that he died there.
verses.10:19: And when all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been routed before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Arameans feared to help the sons of Ammon anymore.
verses.11:1: Now it came to pass at the return of the year, at the time when kings go forth, that David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they laid waste the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David remained at Jerusalem.
verses.11:2: And it came to pass at the time of evening that David arose from his bed and walked upon the roof of the king's house; and from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was exceedingly fair in appearance.
verses.11:3: So David sent and inquired about the woman. And one said, "Is this not Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
verses.11:4: Then David sent messengers and took her; and she came to him, and he lay with her, for she was purifying herself from her uncleanness. Then she returned to her house.
verses.11:5: And the woman conceived; so she sent and told David, saying, "I am with child."
verses.11:6: Then David sent word to Joab, "Send Uriah the Hittite to me." So Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.11:7: When Uriah came to him, David inquired after the welfare of Joab, and the welfare of the people, and how the war prospered.
verses.11:8: And David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." So Uriah departed from the king's house, and a gift from the king followed after him.
verses.11:9: But Uriah lay down at the entrance of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.
verses.11:10: When they told David, saying, "Uriah did not go down to his house," David said to Uriah, "Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?"
verses.11:11: And Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah abide in booths, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped upon the open field. Shall I then enter my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing!"
verses.11:12: Then David said to Uriah, "Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away." So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the next day.
verses.11:13: And David invited him, and he ate and drank before him, and David made him drunk. Yet in the evening he went out to lie upon his bed with the servants of his lord, and to his house he did not go down.
verses.11:14: And it came to pass in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.11:15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, "Set Uriah in the forefront of the fiercest battle, and draw back from behind him, that he may be struck down and die."
verses.11:16: So it came to pass, as Joab was watching the city, that he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew that men of valor were.
verses.11:17: And the men of the city came out and fought with Joab; and some of the people, of the servants of David, fell, and Uriah the Hittite died also.
verses.11:18: Then Joab sent and reported to David all the events of the battle.
verses.11:19: And he commanded the messenger, saying, "When you have finished telling all the events of the battle to the king,
verses.11:20: then it shall be, if the wrath of the king rises and he says to you, 'Why did you draw so near to the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?
verses.11:21: Who struck down Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman cast an upper millstone upon him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you draw near to the wall?' then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.'"
verses.11:22: So the messenger went, and came and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to tell.
verses.11:23: And the messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us and came out against us into the field, and we pressed upon them as far as the entrance of the gate.
verses.11:24: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king's servants died; and your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also."
verses.11:25: Then David said to the messenger, "Thus you shall say to Joab, 'Do not let this thing be evil in your sight, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your battle against the city and overthrow it.' So encourage him."
verses.11:26: When the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she lamented over her husband.
verses.11:27: And when the time of mourning was past, David sent and brought her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.12:1: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David. And he came to him and said to him, "There were two men in one city, the one rich and the other poor.
verses.12:2: The rich man had flocks and herds in exceeding abundance.
verses.12:3: But the poor man had nothing at all, except one small ewe lamb which he had bought and reared; and it grew up together with him and with his children. It would eat of his own morsel and drink from his own cup and lie in his bosom, and it was to him like a daughter.
verses.12:4: Now a wayfarer came to the rich man, and he was unwilling to take from his own flock or from his own herd to prepare for the traveler who had come to him; but he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
verses.12:5: Then David's anger was kindled exceedingly against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who has done this is worthy of death!
verses.12:6: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he showed no pity."
verses.12:7: Then Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I anointed you as king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul.
verses.12:8: And I gave you the house of your master and the wives of your master into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if that were too little, I would also have added to you as much again and more.
verses.12:9: Why have you despised the word of the LORD, to do what is evil in My sight? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword; you have taken his wife to be your wife, and him you have slain by the sword of the sons of Ammon.
verses.12:10: Now therefore, the sword shall not depart from your house forever, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'
verses.12:11: Thus says the LORD: 'Behold, I am raising up calamity against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
verses.12:12: For you acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.'"
verses.12:13: Then David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." And Nathan said to David, "The LORD also has taken away your sin; you shall not die.
verses.12:14: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have given the enemies of the LORD great occasion to blaspheme, the son also who is born to you shall surely die."
verses.12:15: Then Nathan departed to his house. And the LORD struck the child whom Uriah's wife bore to David, and he became grievously ill.
verses.12:16: Therefore David sought God on behalf of the child; and David kept a fast, and went in and passed the night lying upon the ground.
verses.12:17: And the elders of his house stood over him to raise him up from the ground, but he was unwilling, nor would he eat bread with them.
verses.12:18: Now it came to pass on the seventh day that the child died. And the servants of David were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "Behold, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to our voice. How then can we say to him, 'The child is dead'? He may do himself harm!"
verses.12:19: When David saw that his servants were whispering among themselves, David perceived that the child was dead. Therefore David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."
verses.12:20: Then David arose from the ground, washed and anointed himself, and changed his garments; and he went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Afterward he came to his own house, and when he asked, they set food before him, and he ate.
verses.12:21: Then his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? For the sake of the child while he was alive you fasted and wept, but when the child died, you arose and ate bread."
verses.12:22: And he said, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, 'Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me, that the child may live.'
verses.12:23: But now he is dead; why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me."
verses.12:24: Then David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her and lay with her; and she bore a son, and she called his name Solomon. And the LORD loved him.
verses.12:25: And He sent word by the hand of Nathan the prophet, who called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.
verses.12:26: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and captured the royal city.
verses.12:27: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, "I have fought against Rabbah, and I have also captured the city of waters.
verses.12:28: Now therefore, gather the rest of the people together, encamp against the city, and capture it, lest I myself capture the city and my name be called over it."
verses.12:29: So David gathered all the people together and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and captured it.
verses.12:30: And he took the crown of their king from off his head; its weight was a talent of gold, with precious stones, and it was placed upon David's head. Also he brought out the spoil of the city in exceedingly great abundance.
verses.12:31: And he brought out the people who were in it, and set them to the saw, and to iron picks, and to iron axes, and made them serve at the brickkiln. Thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:1: Now it came to pass after this that Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
verses.13:2: And Amnon was so distressed that he made himself sick on account of Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
verses.13:3: Now Amnon had a companion whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
verses.13:4: And he said to him, "Why are you, the king's son, growing so gaunt morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother."
verses.13:5: Then Jonadab said to him, "Lie down upon your bed and feign yourself ill; and when your father comes to see you, you shall say to him, 'Please let Tamar my sister come and give me food to eat, and prepare the fare in my sight, that I may see it and eat from her hand.'"
verses.13:6: So Amnon lay down and feigned himself ill; and when the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let Tamar my sister come and make two cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand."
verses.13:7: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, "Go now to the house of Amnon your brother, and prepare food for him."
verses.13:8: So Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And she took dough and kneaded it, and shaped cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.
verses.13:9: Then she took the pan and poured them out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Have every man go out from my presence." So every man went out from his presence.
verses.13:10: Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner chamber, that I may eat from your hand." So Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the inner chamber to Amnon her brother.
verses.13:11: Now when she brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
verses.13:12: But she said to him, "No, my brother, do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel! Do not commit this disgraceful folly.
verses.13:13: And I, where could I carry my reproach? And as for you, you would be like one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
verses.13:14: Yet he would not listen to her voice; and being stronger than she, he violated her and lay with her.
verses.13:15: Then Amnon hated her with an exceedingly great hatred, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Arise, be gone!"
verses.13:16: And she said to him, "No! For this evil in sending me away is greater than the other that you have done to me." Yet he would not listen to her.
verses.13:17: Then he called his young man who attended him, and said, "Send this woman out from my presence now, and bolt the door behind her."
verses.13:18: Now she was wearing a tunic of many colors, for in such robes the virgin daughters of the king were attired. And his attendant brought her outside, and bolted the door behind her.
verses.13:19: Then Tamar put ashes upon her head, and tore the tunic of many colors that was on her; and she laid her hand upon her head and went away, crying out aloud as she went.
verses.13:20: And Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now therefore, my sister, hold your peace; he is your brother. Do not take this matter to heart." So Tamar dwelt desolate in the house of Absalom her brother.
verses.13:21: Now when King David heard of all these things, he was exceedingly angry.
verses.13:22: And Absalom spoke to Amnon neither bad nor good; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had violated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:23: And it came to pass after two full years that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
verses.13:24: Then Absalom came to the king and said, "Behold now, your servant has sheepshearers; please let the king and his servants go with your servant."
verses.13:25: But the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be a burden upon you." And he urged him, yet he would not go, but blessed him.
verses.13:26: Then Absalom said, "If not, please let Amnon my brother go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
verses.13:27: Yet Absalom urged him, so he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him.
verses.13:28: Now Absalom had commanded his young men, saying, "Watch now, when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then put him to death. Do not fear; have I not commanded you? Be strong and be men of valor!"
verses.13:29: So the young men of Absalom did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and every man mounted his mule and fled.
verses.13:30: And it came to pass, while they were on the way, that the report came to David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them is left!"
verses.13:31: Then the king arose, tore his garments, and lay upon the ground; and all his servants stood by with their garments torn.
verses.13:32: Then Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered and said, "Do not let my lord suppose that they have slain all the young men, the king's sons, for Amnon alone is dead; for by the command of Absalom this has been determined from the day he violated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:33: Now therefore, do not let my lord the king take the matter to heart, thinking, 'All the king's sons are dead,' for Amnon alone is dead."
verses.13:34: Meanwhile Absalom fled. And the young man who kept watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming along the road behind him, from the side of the mountain.
verses.13:35: Then Jonadab said to the king, "Behold, the king's sons have come! According to the word of your servant, so it has come to pass."
verses.13:36: And it came to pass, as soon as he had finished speaking, that behold, the king's sons arrived, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and the king also and all his servants wept with an exceedingly great weeping.
verses.13:37: And Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
verses.13:38: So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
verses.13:39: And the spirit of King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.
verses.14:1: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah knew that the heart of the king was toward Absalom.
verses.14:2: And Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman, and he said to her, "Please act as a mourner, and please put on garments of mourning, and do not anoint yourself with oil, but be as a woman who has mourned these many days for the dead.
verses.14:3: And come to the king and speak to him according to this word." So Joab placed the words in her mouth.
verses.14:4: And when the Tekoite woman spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the earth and bowed down, and said, "Help, O king!"
verses.14:5: And the king said to her, "What troubles you?" And she answered, "Truly I am a widow woman, for my husband is dead.
verses.14:6: And your maidservant had two sons, and the two of them strove together in the field, and there was no deliverer between them; so the one struck the other and slew him.
verses.14:7: And behold, the whole family has risen up against your maidservant, and they said, 'Deliver up the one who struck his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also.' Thus they would quench my coal that remains, so as to leave to my husband neither name nor remnant upon the face of the earth."
verses.14:8: Then the king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give a command concerning you."
verses.14:9: And the Tekoite woman said to the king, "My lord the king, let the iniquity be upon me and upon my father's house, and let the king and his throne be guiltless."
verses.14:10: And the king said, "Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he shall not touch you any longer."
verses.14:11: Then she said, "Please let the king remember the LORD your God, that the avenger of blood may not multiply destruction, lest they destroy my son." And he said, "As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
verses.14:12: Then the woman said, "Please let your maidservant speak a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."
verses.14:13: And the woman said, "Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is as one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring back his banished one.
verses.14:14: For we shall surely die, and are like water poured out upon the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. Yet God does not take away a life, but He devises plans so that one who is banished may not remain cast out from Him.
verses.14:15: Now therefore, I have come to speak this word to my lord the king because the people made me afraid. And your maidservant said, 'Please let me speak to the king; perhaps the king will perform the word of his handmaid.
verses.14:16: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid from the hand of the man who seeks to destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God.'
verses.14:17: And your maidservant said, 'Please let the word of my lord the king be for rest, for as the angel of God, so is my lord the king to hear the good and the evil.' And may the LORD your God be with you."
verses.14:18: Then the king answered and said to the woman, "Please do not conceal from me anything that I am about to ask you." And the woman said, "Please let my lord the king speak."
verses.14:19: And the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman answered and said, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken. For your servant Joab, he commanded me, and he placed all these words in the mouth of your maidservant.
verses.14:20: To turn about the face of the matter your servant Joab has done this thing; yet my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of the angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth."
verses.14:21: And the king said to Joab, "Behold now, I have granted this thing; go therefore, bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.14:22: Then Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and blessed the king. And Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has fulfilled the word of your servant."
verses.14:23: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.14:24: And the king said, "Let him turn aside to his own house, and let him not see my face." So Absalom turned aside to his own house, and did not see the king's face.
verses.14:25: Now in all Israel there was no man so handsome as Absalom, to be so greatly praised; from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.14:26: And when he cut the hair of his head—for at the end of every year he would cut it, because it was heavy upon him, therefore he cut it—he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
verses.14:27: And to Absalom were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar; she was a woman of fair appearance.
verses.14:28: So Absalom dwelt in Jerusalem two full years, yet he did not see the king's face.
verses.14:29: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he was not willing to come to him. And he sent again a second time, but he was not willing to come.
verses.14:30: So he said to his servants, "See, Joab's field is beside mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
verses.14:31: Then Joab arose and came to Absalom at his house, and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"
verses.14:32: And Absalom said to Joab, "Behold, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, that I may send you to the king,' to say, 'Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still.' Now therefore, let me see the king's face; and if there is iniquity in me, let him put me to death."
verses.14:33: So Joab came to the king and told him. And when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.
verses.15:1: Now it came to pass after this that Absalom prepared for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.15:2: And Absalom would rise early and stand beside the way to the gate. So it was, whenever any man who had a lawsuit came to the king for judgment, that Absalom would call to him and say, "From what city are you?" And he would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.15:3: Then Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, yet there is no one from the king to hear you."
verses.15:4: Moreover Absalom would say, "Oh, that someone would appoint me judge in the land, that every man who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would give him justice!"
verses.15:5: And so it was, whenever any man drew near to bow down to him, that he would stretch out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.
verses.15:6: In this manner Absalom acted toward all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the heart of the men of Israel.
verses.15:7: Now it came to pass at the end of forty years that Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.
verses.15:8: For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelt at Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If the LORD indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.'"
verses.15:9: And the king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.
verses.15:10: Then Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, 'Absalom reigns in Hebron!'"
verses.15:11: And with Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who were invited, and they went in their innocence, and did not know anything.
verses.15:12: Then Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city, from Giloh, while he offered the sacrifices. And the conspiracy grew strong, for the people with Absalom continually increased in number.
verses.15:13: Now a messenger came to David, saying, "The heart of the men of Israel has turned after Absalom."
verses.15:14: So David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, and let us flee, for otherwise we shall have no escape from Absalom. Make haste to depart, lest he overtake us quickly and bring calamity upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.15:15: And the king's servants said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king shall choose, behold, your servants are ready."
verses.15:16: So the king went out with all his household following after him; but the king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.
verses.15:17: And the king went out with all the people following him, and they halted at the farthest house.
verses.15:18: And all his servants passed by beside him, and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites—six hundred men who had followed him from Gath—passed on before the king.
verses.15:19: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you also go with us? Return and remain with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.
verses.15:20: You came only yesterday, and today should I make you wander up and down with us, seeing I go wherever I may go? Return, and take your brethren back with you; mercy and truth be with you."
verses.15:21: And Ittai answered the king and said, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in whatever place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or in life, even there shall your servant be."
verses.15:22: So David said to Ittai, "Go, and cross over." Then Ittai the Gittite crossed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.
verses.15:23: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people crossed over. The king himself also crossed over the Brook Kidron, and all the people crossed over toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.15:24: And behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
verses.15:25: Then the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and show me both it and His habitation.
verses.15:26: But if He says thus, 'I have no delight in you,' behold, here I am; let Him do to me as seems good in His eyes."
verses.15:27: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
verses.15:28: See, I will wait in the plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
verses.15:29: Therefore Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.
verses.15:30: So David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered and went barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
verses.15:31: Then someone told David, saying, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "O LORD, I pray, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."
verses.15:32: Now it came to pass, when David had come to the summit where God was worshiped, that behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn and earth upon his head.
verses.15:33: And David said to him, "If you pass on with me, then you will be a burden to me.
verses.15:34: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I have been your father's servant in time past, so now I will also be your servant,' then you may defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.15:35: And are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Therefore it shall be that whatever word you hear from the king's house, you shall tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.15:36: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok's son, and Jonathan, Abiathar's son; and by their hand you shall send to me everything that you hear."
verses.15:37: So Hushai, David's friend, went into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
verses.16:1: Now David had passed a little beyond the summit, and behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth came to meet him with a pair of saddled donkeys, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred clusters of raisins, one hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
verses.16:2: Then the king said to Ziba, "What do you mean by these?" And Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for the weary to drink in the wilderness."
verses.16:3: Then the king said, "And where is your master's son?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he remains in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"
verses.16:4: So the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down; may I find favor in your sight, my lord the king."
verses.16:5: Now when King David came as far as Bahurim, behold, a man from the family of the house of Saul came out from there, whose name was Shimei the son of Gera; he came forth, cursing continually as he came.
verses.16:6: And he cast stones at David and at all the servants of King David, though all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
verses.16:7: And thus Shimei spoke as he cursed: "Get out, get out, you man of blood and worthless man!
verses.16:8: The LORD has brought back upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. And behold, you are in your own calamity, because you are a man of blood!"
verses.16:9: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head."
verses.16:10: But the king said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? So let him curse, because the LORD has said to him, 'Curse David.' Who then shall say, 'Why have you done this?'"
verses.16:11: And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Behold, my son who came forth from my own body seeks my life; how much more now may this Benjamite! Leave him alone, and let him curse, for the LORD has spoken to him.
verses.16:12: Perhaps the LORD will look upon my eye, and the LORD will repay me good in return for his cursing this day."
verses.16:13: So David and his men went along the road, while Shimei walked along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went, casting stones toward him, and flinging dust.
verses.16:14: And the king and all the people who were with him arrived weary, and he refreshed himself there.
verses.16:15: Meanwhile Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
verses.16:16: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, the friend of David, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
verses.16:17: So Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
verses.16:18: And Hushai said to Absalom, "No, rather, the one whom the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, his I will be, and with him I will abide.
verses.16:19: And secondly, whom should I serve? Should it not be before his son? As I have served before your father, so will I be before you."
verses.16:20: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel: what shall we do?"
verses.16:21: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house; and all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."
verses.16:22: So they pitched a tent for Absalom upon the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.16:23: Now the counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in those days, was as when a man inquires of the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
verses.17:1: Moreover Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Please let me choose twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue David tonight.
verses.17:2: I will come upon him while he is weary and weak of hands, and I will throw him into terror; then all the people who are with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone.
verses.17:3: Then I will bring back all the people to you; the return of everyone depends upon the man whom you seek, and all the people will be at peace."
verses.17:4: And the saying seemed right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
verses.17:5: Then Absalom said, "Please call Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear what is in his mouth as well."
verses.17:6: When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, "Ahithophel has spoken in this manner. Shall we carry out his word? If not, you speak."
verses.17:7: Then Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good at this time."
verses.17:8: Moreover Hushai said, "You know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are bitter of soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. And your father is a man of war, and he will not lodge with the people.
verses.17:9: Behold, even now he is hidden in one of the pits or in some other place. And it will come to pass, when some fall among them at the outset, that whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'
verses.17:10: And even the valiant man, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and that those who are with him are men of valor.
verses.17:11: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be surely gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand that is by the sea for multitude, and that you yourself go forth into battle.
verses.17:12: Then we will come upon him in one of the places where he may be found, and we will settle upon him as the dew falls upon the ground; and of him and of all the men who are with him, not even one shall be left.
verses.17:13: Moreover, if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel shall bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it into the valley until not even a pebble is found there."
verses.17:14: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel, in order that the LORD might bring disaster upon Absalom.
verses.17:15: Then Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, "Thus and thus Ahithophel has counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I have counseled.
verses.17:16: Now therefore, send quickly and tell David, saying, 'Do not lodge tonight in the plains of the wilderness, but by all means cross over, lest the king and all the people who are with him be swallowed up.'"
verses.17:17: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En Rogel; and a maidservant went and told them, and they were to go and tell King David, for they could not let themselves be seen entering the city.
verses.17:18: However, a young man saw them and told Absalom. So both of them went away quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his courtyard; and they went down into it.
verses.17:19: Then the woman took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered crushed grain upon it; and the matter was not known.
verses.17:20: When the servants of Absalom came to the woman at the house, they said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have crossed over the brook of water." So they searched, and when they did not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.17:21: And it came to pass, after they had gone, that they came up out of the well and went and told King David. And they said to David, "Arise and cross over the water quickly, for thus has Ahithophel counseled against you."
verses.17:22: Then David and all the people who were with him arose and crossed over the Jordan. By morning light, not even one was missing who had not crossed over the Jordan.
verses.17:23: Now when Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been carried out, he saddled his donkey, arose, and went to his house, to his own city. Then he set his household in order and hanged himself, and died; and he was buried in his father's tomb.
verses.17:24: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom crossed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.17:25: And Absalom set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab.
verses.17:26: So Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
verses.17:27: Now it came to pass, when David had come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,
verses.17:28: brought beds and basins, earthen vessels and wheat, barley and flour, parched grain and beans, lentils and parched seeds,
verses.17:29: honey and curds, sheep and cheese of the herd, to David and to the people who were with him to eat; for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."
verses.18:1: And David mustered the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
verses.18:2: Then David sent out the people: one third under the hand of Joab, one third under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, and one third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "I also will surely go out with you."
verses.18:3: But the people answered, "You shall not go out! For if we indeed flee, they will not give a thought to us; and if half of us perish, they will not care about us. For now you are worth ten thousand of us; therefore now it is better that you be ready to aid us from the city."
verses.18:4: And the king said to them, "Whatever seems good in your eyes I will do." So the king stood beside the gate, while all the people marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.18:5: Now the king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom." And all the people heard when the king charged all the captains concerning Absalom.
verses.18:6: So the people went out into the field to meet Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
verses.18:7: There the people of Israel were defeated before the servants of David, and the slaughter there on that day was great—twenty thousand.
verses.18:8: For the battle there spread out over the face of all the countryside, and the forest devoured more of the people than the sword devoured on that day.
verses.18:9: Then Absalom chanced to encounter the servants of David. Now Absalom was riding on a mule, and the mule went beneath the thick boughs of a great terebinth tree, and his head caught fast in the terebinth; so he was left hanging between heaven and earth, while the mule that was under him went on.
verses.18:10: And a certain man saw it and reported to Joab, saying, "Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in a terebinth tree!"
verses.18:11: Then Joab said to the man who had told him, "Behold, you saw him! Why then did you not strike him down to the ground there? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a belt."
verses.18:12: But the man said to Joab, "Even though I were to weigh a thousand pieces of silver into my palms, I would not stretch forth my hand against the king's son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Take care, whoever you are, of the young man Absalom!'
