verses.18:13: Otherwise I would have dealt treacherously against my own life—for nothing is hidden from the king—and you yourself would have stood aloof."
verses.18:14: Then Joab said, "I will not linger thus before you." And he took three javelins in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the terebinth tree.
verses.18:15: And ten young men who bore Joab's armor surrounded Absalom, and struck him and slew him.
verses.18:16: Then Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab restrained the people.
verses.18:17: And they took Absalom and cast him into the great pit in the forest, and heaped a very great pile of stones over him. Meanwhile all Israel fled, every man to his tent.
verses.18:18: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself a pillar, which is in the King's Valley; for he had said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He called the pillar after his own name, and to this day it is called Absalom's Monument.
verses.18:19: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Please let me run and bring tidings to the king, that the LORD has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies."
verses.18:20: And Joab said to him, "You shall not be a bearer of tidings today, but you may bear tidings on another day. Today you shall bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead."
verses.18:21: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." So the Cushite bowed low to Joab and ran.
verses.18:22: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok spoke yet again to Joab, saying, "Come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why would you run, my son, since no reward for the tidings awaits you?"
verses.18:23: "Come what may, I will run." So he said to him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
verses.18:24: Now David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man was running alone.
verses.18:25: Then the watchman cried out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, there are tidings in his mouth." And he kept coming nearer and nearer.
verses.18:26: Then the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, "Behold, a man is running alone!" And the king said, "This one also brings tidings."
verses.18:27: And the watchman said, "I observe that the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "He is a good man, and he comes with good tidings."
verses.18:28: Then Ahimaaz cried out and said to the king, "All is well!" And he bowed down before the king with his face to the earth, and said, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king!"
verses.18:29: And the king asked, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" And Ahimaaz answered, "I saw a great tumult when Joab sent the king's servant and your servant, but I did not know what it was."
verses.18:30: And the king said, "Turn aside and stand here." So he turned aside and stood still.
verses.18:31: And behold, the Cushite arrived; and the Cushite said, "Let my lord the king receive tidings, for the LORD has vindicated you this day from the hand of all those who rose up against you."
verses.18:32: And the king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" And the Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against you for evil, be like that young man!"
verses.19:1: Then the king was deeply shaken, and went up to the upper chamber over the gate, and wept. And as he went, thus he said: "O my son Absalom—my son, my son Absalom! Would that I myself had died in your place! O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.19:2: And it was told to Joab, "Behold, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."
verses.19:3: So the victory on that day was turned into mourning for all the people, because the people heard it said on that day, "The king is grieved for his son."
verses.19:4: And the people stole into the city on that day, just as people who are put to shame steal away when they flee in battle.
verses.19:5: Now the king had covered his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.19:6: Then Joab came into the house to the king and said, "Today you have put to shame the faces of all your servants, who today have delivered your life, and the lives of your sons and your daughters, and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines,
verses.19:7: by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For you have declared today that commanders and servants mean nothing to you; for today I perceive that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then it would have been pleasing in your sight.
verses.19:8: Now therefore, arise, go out and speak kindly to your servants. For I swear by the LORD, if you do not go out, not a single man will remain with you tonight; and that will be worse for you than all the calamity that has come upon you from your youth until now."
verses.19:9: So the king arose and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, saying, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." Then all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, every man to his tent.
verses.19:10: And all the people were in dispute throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies, and he rescued us from the hand of the Philistines; yet now he has fled from the land because of Absalom.
verses.19:11: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now therefore, why do you remain silent about bringing back the king?"
verses.19:12: Then King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, since the word of all Israel has come to the king, even to his house?
verses.19:13: You are my brethren; you are my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?'
verses.19:14: And say to Amasa, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God do so to me, and more also, if you are not commander of the army before me continually in the place of Joab.'"
verses.19:15: So he swayed the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they sent word to the king: "Return, you and all your servants."
verses.19:16: Then the king returned and came to the Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.
verses.19:17: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite who was from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
verses.19:18: There were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they rushed across the Jordan before the king.
verses.19:19: And a ferryboat crossed over to bring over the king's household and to do what was good in his sight. Now Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king as he was about to cross the Jordan,
verses.19:20: and said to the king, "Do not let my lord impute iniquity to me, nor remember the wrong your servant committed on the day that my lord the king departed from Jerusalem, that the king should take it to heart.
verses.19:21: For your servant knows that I have sinned; therefore, behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph, to go down to meet my lord the king."
verses.19:22: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Should not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?"
verses.19:23: And David said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should become adversaries to me today? Shall any man be put to death today in Israel? For do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"
verses.19:24: Therefore the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king swore to him.
verses.19:25: Now Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. And he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his mustache, nor washed his garments, from the day the king departed until the day he came back in peace.
verses.19:26: And it came to pass, when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.19:27: And he answered, "My lord, O king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, 'I will saddle a donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go with the king,' because your servant is lame.
verses.19:28: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God; therefore do what is good in your sight.
verses.19:29: For all my father's house were nothing but dead men before my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your own table. What right, therefore, do I still have to cry out any more to the king?"
verses.19:30: Then the king said to him, "Why do you speak any more of your matters? I have said: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
verses.19:31: And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Rather, let him take it all, since my lord the king has come back in peace to his own house."
verses.19:32: Now Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went across the Jordan with the king, to escort him over the Jordan.
verses.19:33: Now Barzillai was very aged, eighty years old; and he had sustained the king while he abode at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
verses.19:34: And the king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I will sustain you with me in Jerusalem."
verses.19:35: But Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
verses.19:36: I am eighty years old today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a burden any longer to my lord the king?
verses.19:37: Your servant will go a little way across the Jordan with the king; and why should the king repay me with such a reward?
verses.19:38: Please let your servant turn back, that I may die in my own city, near the grave of my father and my mother. Yet behold, here is your servant Chimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight."
verses.19:39: And the king answered, "Chimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your sight; and whatever you desire of me, I will do for you."
verses.19:40: Then all the people crossed over the Jordan, and the king crossed over. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.
verses.19:41: Now the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him; and all the people of Judah escorted the king across, and also half the people of Israel.
verses.19:42: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, "Why have our brethren, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan, and all David's men with him?"
verses.19:43: So all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is near of kin to us. Why then are you angry over this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king's expense, or has any gift been bestowed upon us?"
verses.19:44: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, "We have ten shares in the king, and we also have more right in David than you. Why then did you despise us? Was not our word the first to bring back our king?" Yet the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
verses.20:1: Now there happened to be there a worthless man, whose name was Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite. And he blew the trumpet and said, "We have no share in David, nor do we have an inheritance in the son of Jesse; every man to his tents, O Israel!"
verses.20:2: So all the men of Israel withdrew from following David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clung steadfastly to their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.
verses.20:3: Now David came to his house at Jerusalem. And the king took the ten women, his concubines whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a guarded house and sustained them, but did not go in to them. So they were shut up until the day of their death, living in widowhood.
verses.20:4: Then the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah for me within three days, and be present here yourself."
verses.20:5: So Amasa went to summon Judah; but he delayed longer than the appointed time which he had appointed for him.
verses.20:6: And David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, lest he find for himself fortified cities and escape from our sight."
verses.20:7: So Joab's men went out after him, with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.20:8: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Now Joab was dressed in his battle garment, and over it was a belt with a sword fastened upon his waist in its sheath; and as he stepped forward, it fell out.
verses.20:9: Then Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" And Joab's right hand took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.
verses.20:10: But Amasa did not guard against the sword that was in Joab's hand; so he struck him with it in the belly and poured out his inward parts to the ground, and did not strike him a second time; and he died. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.20:11: And one of Joab's young men stood beside him and said, "Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David—follow Joab!"
verses.20:12: Now Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he moved Amasa from the highway into the field and threw a garment over him, when he saw that everyone who came upon him stopped.
verses.20:13: When he had been removed from the highway, all the men passed on after Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.20:14: And he passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth Maachah, and all the Berites; and they gathered together and also went after him.
verses.20:15: Then they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth Maachah; and they cast up a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart. And all the people who were with Joab were battering the wall to throw it down.
verses.20:16: Then a wise woman cried out from the city, "Hear, hear! Please say to Joab, 'Come near here, that I may speak with you.'"
verses.20:17: When he came near to her, the woman said, "Are you Joab?" And he answered, "I am." Then she said to him, "Hear the words of your maidservant." And he answered, "I am listening."
verses.20:18: So she spoke, saying, "In former times they used to speak, saying, 'Let them surely seek counsel at Abel,' and thus they would end a matter.
verses.20:19: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?"
verses.20:20: And Joab answered and said, "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy!
verses.20:21: The matter is not so. Rather, a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against the king, even against David. Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city." And the woman said to Joab, "Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall."
verses.20:22: Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. Then he blew the trumpet, and they dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to the king at Jerusalem.
verses.20:23: Now Joab was over all the army of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;
verses.20:24: Adoram was over the forced labor; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder;
verses.20:25: Sheva was scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were the priests;
verses.20:26: and Ira the Jairite was also a priest to David.
verses.21:1: Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year; and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, "It is on account of Saul and the house of bloodguilt, because he put the Gibeonites to death."
verses.21:2: So the king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn to them, yet Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.
verses.21:3: And David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?"
verses.21:4: And the Gibeonites said to him, "We have no matter of silver or gold with Saul or with his house, nor is it ours to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "Whatever you say, I will do for you."
verses.21:5: So they said to the king, "As for the man who consumed us and who schemed against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any territory of Israel,
verses.21:6: let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD." And the king said, "I will give them."
verses.21:7: But the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
verses.21:8: So the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
verses.21:9: And he delivered them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain before the LORD. So all seven of them fell together, and they were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.21:10: Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured upon them from the heavens; and she did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest upon them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
verses.21:11: And it was reported to David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
verses.21:12: So David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the open square of Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hanged them on the day the Philistines struck down Saul at Gilboa.
verses.21:13: And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.
verses.21:14: And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father; and they did all that the king commanded. And after that, God heeded the plea for the land.
verses.21:15: Now the Philistines had war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines, and David grew weary.
verses.21:16: Then Ishbi-Benob, who was of the descendants of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and who was girded with a new sword, purposed to strike down David.
verses.21:17: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid, and struck the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, "You shall no longer go out with us to battle, lest you quench the lamp of Israel."
verses.21:18: Now it came to pass afterward that there was war again with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was of the descendants of the giant.
verses.21:19: And there was war again with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan the son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
verses.21:20: And there was war again at Gath, and there was a man of great stature whose fingers on his hands and toes on his feet were six on each, twenty-four in number; and he also was born to the giant.
verses.21:21: And when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimeah, the brother of David, struck him down.
verses.21:22: These four were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
verses.22:1: And David spoke to the LORD the words of this song in the day the LORD rescued him from the grasp of all his enemies and from the grasp of Saul.
verses.22:2: And he said, "The LORD is my crag and my stronghold, and my own deliverer;
verses.22:3: the God of my rock, in Him I take refuge—my shield and the horn of my salvation, my high tower and my shelter, my Savior; from violence You save me.
verses.22:4: I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and from my enemies I shall be saved.
verses.22:5: For the breakers of death encompassed me; the torrents of ruin filled me with dread.
verses.22:6: The cords of Sheol encircled me; the snares of death closed in upon me.
verses.22:7: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and to my God I called out; and from His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for help entered His ears.
verses.22:8: Then the earth reeled and quaked; the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, because His anger burned.
verses.22:9: Smoke ascended from His nostrils, and fire from His mouth devoured; burning coals blazed forth from Him.
verses.22:10: He bent the heavens and descended, and thick darkness lay beneath His feet.
verses.22:11: He rode upon a cherub and flew, and He was seen upon the wings of the wind.
verses.22:12: He set darkness around Himself as pavilions—a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
verses.22:13: Out of the radiance before Him, coals of fire were kindled.
verses.22:14: The LORD thundered from the heavens, and the Most High gave forth His voice.
verses.22:15: He sent forth arrows and scattered them—lightning, and brought confusion.
verses.22:16: Then the channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
verses.22:17: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me out of many waters.
verses.22:18: He delivered me from my mighty enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me.
verses.22:19: They came against me in the day of my calamity, yet the LORD became my stay.
verses.22:20: He brought me forth into a spacious place; He rescued me because He delighted in me.
verses.22:21: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the purity of my hands He repaid me.
verses.22:22: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not turned wickedly away from my God.
verses.22:23: For all His ordinances were before me, and from His statutes I did not turn aside.
verses.22:24: I was blameless toward Him, and I guarded myself from my iniquity.
verses.22:25: So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my purity before His eyes.
verses.22:26: With the faithful You show Yourself faithful; with the blameless mighty man You show Yourself blameless;
verses.22:27: with the pure You show Yourself pure, and with the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.
verses.22:28: An afflicted people You save, but Your eyes are upon the haughty, whom You bring low.
verses.22:29: For You are my lamp, O LORD, and the LORD brightens my darkness.
verses.22:30: For by You I can charge against a troop; by my God I can leap over a wall.
verses.22:31: As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is refined; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
verses.22:32: For who is God apart from the LORD? And who is a rock apart from our God?
verses.22:33: God is my mighty stronghold, and He guides my way blamelessly.
verses.22:34: He makes my feet like the feet of deer, and causes me to stand upon my high places.
verses.22:35: He trains my hands for battle, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
verses.22:36: You have given me the shield of Your salvation, and Your gentleness has made me great.
verses.22:37: You widened my stride beneath me, and my ankles did not slip.
verses.22:38: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I did not turn back until they were consumed.
verses.22:39: I consumed them and struck them down so that they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.
verses.22:40: You girded me with strength for battle; You brought down beneath me those who rose up against me.
verses.22:41: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and those who hated me I cut off.
verses.22:42: They looked around, but there was no one to save—even to the LORD, yet He did not answer them.
verses.22:43: I ground them fine as the dust of the earth; like the mire of the streets I crushed them and trampled them down.
verses.22:44: You rescued me from the strivings of my people; You preserved me as the head of the nations; a people I did not know shall serve me.
verses.22:45: Foreigners cringe in submission to me; at the hearing of the ear they obey me.
verses.22:46: Foreigners fade away and come limping out of their strongholds.
verses.22:47: The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock! May God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted!
verses.22:48: He is the God who grants me vengeance and brings down peoples beneath me,
verses.22:49: who brings me out from my enemies; You also lift me up above those who rise against me, and from the man of violence You rescue me.
verses.22:50: Therefore I will give thanks to You, O LORD, among the nations, and to Your name I will sing praises.
verses.22:51: He is a tower of salvation to His king, and shows lovingkindness to His anointed, to David and to his descendants forever."
verses.23:1: Now these are the last words of David: The oracle of David the son of Jesse, and the oracle of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet singer of the psalms of Israel:
verses.23:2: "The Spirit of the LORD has spoken through me, and His word is on my tongue.
verses.23:3: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, 'He who rules over mankind righteously, who rules in the fear of God,
verses.23:4: is like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, bringing tender grass from the earth through brightness after rain.'
verses.23:5: Is not my house indeed thus with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and secure. For all my salvation and every desire—will He not cause it to spring forth?
verses.23:6: Yet worthless men are all of them like thorns thrust aside, for they cannot be taken with the hand;
verses.23:7: rather, the man who touches them must be armed with iron and the shaft of a spear, and they shall be utterly burned with fire right in their place."
verses.23:8: These are the names of the mighty men who belonged to David: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the captains; he was also called Adino the Eznite, because of eight hundred whom he slew at one time.
verses.23:9: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the son of an Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel had withdrawn.
verses.23:10: He arose and struck down the Philistines until his hand grew weary, and his hand clung to the sword. And the LORD wrought a great deliverance that day; and the people returned after him only to plunder.
verses.23:11: And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. Now the Philistines had gathered together into a troop where there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people fled from before the Philistines.
verses.23:12: But he took his stand in the midst of the plot, defended it, and struck down the Philistines; so the LORD wrought a great deliverance.
verses.23:13: Then three of the thirty chief men went down and came to David at harvest time at the cave of Adullam, while a troop of the Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.23:14: Now David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.
verses.23:15: And David longed and said, "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!"
verses.23:16: So the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. Yet he refused to drink it, and he poured it out to the LORD.
verses.23:17: And he said, "Far be it from me, O LORD, that I should do this! Is this not the blood of the men who went at the peril of their lives?" Therefore he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
verses.23:18: Now Abishai the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief of the three. He brandished his spear against three hundred and slew them, and he had a name among the three.
verses.23:19: Was he not the most honored among the three? Therefore he became their commander; yet he did not attain to the three.
verses.23:20: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, great in exploits, from Kabzeel—he struck down the two lionlike heroes of Moab. He also went down and slew the lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.
verses.23:21: And he struck down an Egyptian, a man of formidable appearance. Now the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, yet he went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.
verses.23:22: These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
verses.23:23: He was more honored than the thirty, yet he did not attain to the three. And David appointed him over his bodyguard.
verses.23:24: Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
verses.23:25: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
verses.23:26: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
verses.23:27: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
verses.23:28: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
verses.23:29: Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
verses.23:30: Benaiah a Pirathonite, Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash,
verses.23:31: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
verses.23:32: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
verses.23:33: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Hararite,
verses.23:34: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
verses.23:35: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
verses.23:36: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
verses.23:37: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armor-bearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
verses.23:38: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
verses.23:39: and Uriah the Hittite—thirty-seven in all.
verses.24:1: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He incited David against them, saying, "Go, number Israel and Judah."
verses.24:2: And the king said to Joab, the commander of the army who was with him, "Pass now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and muster the people, so that I may know the number of the people."
verses.24:3: And Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king look on! Yet why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"
verses.24:4: Yet the word of the king prevailed over Joab and over the commanders of the army. And Joab and the commanders of the army departed from before the king to muster the people of Israel.
verses.24:5: And they crossed over the Jordan and encamped at Aroer, on the south side of the city that is in the middle of the ravine of Gad, and on toward Jazer.
verses.24:6: And they came to Gilead and into the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they arrived at Dan-jaan and around toward Sidon,
verses.24:7: and they came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and of the Canaanites; then they went out to the South of Judah, to Beersheba.
verses.24:8: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
verses.24:9: And Joab gave the sum of the numbering of the people to the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.
verses.24:10: And David's heart struck him after he had numbered the people. So David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done; but now, O LORD, take away, I pray, the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
verses.24:11: Now when David arose in the morning, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,
verses.24:12: "Go and speak to David, 'Thus says the LORD: I hold out three things before you; choose one of them for yourself, that I may do it to you.'"
verses.24:13: So Gad came to David and told him, and he said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come upon you in your land? Or shall you flee three months before your adversaries while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of pestilence in your land? Now consider and see what answer I shall return to Him who sent me."
verses.24:14: And David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall, I pray, into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hand of man."
verses.24:15: So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning until the appointed time; and seventy thousand men of the people died from Dan to Beersheba.
verses.24:16: And when the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented concerning the calamity, and He said to the angel who was bringing destruction among the people, "It is enough! Now stay your hand." And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
verses.24:17: Then David spoke to the LORD when he saw the angel who was striking the people, and he said, "Behold, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father's house."
verses.24:18: And Gad came to David that day and said to him, "Go up, erect an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
verses.24:19: So David went up according to the word of Gad, as the LORD had commanded.
verses.24:20: Now Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him. So Araunah went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.
verses.24:21: And Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" And David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, that the plague may be restrained from the people."
verses.24:22: Then Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up whatever is good in his sight. Behold, here are the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the yokes of the oxen for wood.
verses.24:23: All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept you."
verses.24:24: But the king said to Araunah, "No, for I will surely buy it from you for a price; neither will I offer up to the LORD my God burnt offerings without cost." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
verses.24:25: And David built there an altar to the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD heeded the prayers for the land, and the plague was restrained from Israel.

notes.1:8: The Ketiv reads "and he said," whereas the Qere (translated here) reads "and I said," matching the context of the Amalekite's reply.
notes.1:9: The rare Hebrew noun translated "anguish" occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and may denote agony, convulsion, or dizziness.
notes.1:16: The Ketiv uses the plural "your bloods" (an idiom for bloodguilt), while the Qere (translated here) reads the singular "your blood."
notes.1:18: Literally "Bow," referring to the title of David's lament; the Book of Jashar ("Book of the Upright") is an ancient collection of Hebrew poems also cited in Joshua 10:13.
notes.2:9: The Masoretic Text reads "the Ashurites," referring to a northern Israelite territory or people, perhaps linked with the tribe of Asher.
notes.2:16: Helkath Hazzurim means "Field of Flints" or "Field of Sword-Edges," commemorating the mutual slaughter of the twenty-four combatants.
notes.2:23: The Hebrew term translated "belly" denotes the lower abdomen or midsection.
notes.2:29: The Arabah is the rift valley along the Jordan River; Bithron denotes a rugged ravine or cleft east of the Jordan.
notes.3:2: The Qere reads the Niphal passive form wayyiwwaledu ("were born"), whereas the Ketiv has a shorter consonantal spelling; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.3:3: The Ketiv spells the name Abigal, while the Qere reads the standard form Abigail.
notes.3:15: The Ketiv reads Lush, while the Qere reads Laish, followed here.
notes.3:18: The Masoretic Text reads hoshia (a Hiphil infinitive absolute or third-person perfect), rendered "I will save" in keeping with the first-person divine speech ("My servant", "My people").
notes.3:25: The Ketiv (mevoekha) and the Qere (movaekha) are orthographic variants sharing the same meaning, "your coming in."
notes.3:29: The Hebrew word pelek literally means "spindle" (as in Proverbs 31:19), conveying frailty or disgrace, though some understand it as a crutch or staff.
notes.4:1: Following the Masoretic Text faithfully, Ishbosheth is referred to simply as "Saul's son" in verses 1 and 2.
notes.4:6: Translating the Masoretic Text directly, "as though to fetch wheat" renders the participle phrase loqchey chittim (literally "takers of wheat"), explaining the assassins' pretext for entering the house.
notes.5:2: The Masoretic qere reads the participle with the definite article ("the one leading out"), aligning it with "and bringing in," whereas the ketiv lacks the article.
notes.5:8: Following the Masoretic qere ("who are hated by David's soul"), whereas the ketiv reads an active plural verb ("they hate David's soul"). The Hebrew term rendered "water shaft" denotes a conduit or subterranean passage into the stronghold.
notes.5:20: Baal-perazim means "Lord of Breakthroughs," commemorating the LORD's decisive victory over the Philistines.
notes.5:24: Following the Masoretic qere ("when you hear"), a slight prepositional variation from the ketiv ("in your hearing") with essentially the same temporal sense.
notes.6:2: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "from Baale-judah" (another name for Kiriath-jearim) and emphasizes the ark's holiness by doubling "the Name" before the title "the LORD of hosts."
notes.6:7: The Hebrew word rendered "irreverence" occurs only here in Scripture and denotes a rash act, error, or irreverent offense.
notes.6:8: Perez-uzzah means "Outbreak against Uzzah" or "Breach of Uzzah," echoing the Hebrew verb and noun for the LORD's sudden judgment.
notes.6:19: The Hebrew term rendered "a portion of meat" is rare (occurring only here and in the parallel passage of Chronicles) and has been understood either as a cut of meat or as a date cake.
notes.7:7: The Masoretic Text reads "tribes of Israel," whereas the parallel passage in First Chronicles seventeen six reads "judges of Israel."
notes.7:16: The Masoretic Text reads "before you," addressing David directly, whereas the Septuagint and Syriac read "before Me."
notes.7:19: Hebrew literally "the law of man" or "the instruction for mankind," understood either as David marveling at God's gracious charter for humanity or as a rhetorical exclamation, "Is this the manner of man?"
notes.7:23: The Masoretic Text shifts briefly to the plural "for you" (addressing Israel) and ends literally "from Egypt, nations and its gods."
notes.8:1: "Metheg-ammah" literally means "the bridle of the cubit" or "the bridle of the mother-city," likely denoting a Philistine town or figuratively control of the chief Philistine metropolis.
notes.8:3: The Masoretic consonantal text reads simply "the River," while the traditional Masoretic reading supplies "Euphrates."
notes.8:4: The Masoretic Text reads "one thousand seven hundred horsemen," whereas First Chronicles eighteen four and the Septuagint here read "one thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen."
notes.8:13: The Masoretic Text reads "Aram" (the Arameans), whereas some Hebrew manuscripts, ancient versions, and First Chronicles eighteen twelve read "Edom" (compare verse fourteen).
notes.8:18: Hebrew literally "priests," which in this royal administrative list likely denotes priestly counselors or chief court officials (compare First Chronicles eighteen seventeen).
notes.9:7: "Grandfather" translates Hebrew "father," which commonly refers to a grandfather or forefather.
notes.9:11: The Masoretic Text literally reads "at my table" without repeating a speaker tag; "replied the king" is supplied to mark the king's concluding declaration resuming verse ten.
notes.10:6: Hebrew Aram is rendered Arameans here and throughout the chapter (traditionally translated Syrians in older English versions). Hebrew ish Tov uses the collective singular ish to denote the men of the region of Tob (cf. Judges 11:3).
notes.10:9: Following the Masoretic Qere, "of Israel"; the Ketiv reads "in Israel."
notes.10:18: Hebrew rekhev ("chariots") is used collectively with the verb "slew" to refer to chariot crews or charioteers.
notes.11:1: The Masoretic text spells "kings" with a quiescent aleph, reflecting a scribal orthography while retaining the vocalization hammelakhim ("the kings"; cf. 1 Chronicles 20:1).
notes.11:11: Hebrew sukkot ("booths") refers to temporary shelters constructed by soldiers during a field campaign.
notes.11:21: Jerubbesheth is the Masoretic form of Jerubbaal (Gideon), substituting Hebrew bosheth ("shame") for the element baal (cf. Judges 9:53).
notes.11:25: David's words "be evil in your sight" create a stark Hebrew echo with the narrator's closing judgment in verse 27 that what David had done "was evil in the sight of the LORD."
notes.12:9: The Qere reads 'in My sight' (followed here), whereas the Ketiv reads 'in His sight.'
notes.12:14: The Hebrew literally reads 'the enemies of the LORD,' traditionally recognized as a scribal euphemism avoiding direct mention of scorning the LORD Himself.
notes.12:22: The Qere reads a waw-consecutive perfect ('and the LORD will be gracious to me'), while the Ketiv reads an imperfect ('will the LORD be gracious to me'); both convey David's hope for divine mercy.
notes.12:24: The Qere reads 'and she called' (Bathsheba, followed here), whereas the Ketiv reads 'and he called' (David).
notes.12:31: The Qere reads 'at the brickkiln' (followed here), whereas the Ketiv reads a consonantal form of uncertain meaning; the clause describes assigning Ammonite captives to forced labor.
notes.13:20: The Hebrew here uses the spelling Aminon, generally understood as a contemptuous diminutive of Amnon.
notes.13:33: The Qere omits the conditional particle written in the Ketiv, reading cleanly 'for Amnon alone is dead.'
notes.13:37: The Qere reads 'Ammihud' (followed here), whereas the Ketiv reads 'Ammihur.' The Hebrew subject of 'mourned' is an unexpressed pronoun referring back to King David.
notes.13:39: The Hebrew verb is feminine singular, implicitly referring to the spirit or soul of King David longing to go out to Absalom.
notes.14:7: The Qere reads the infinitive construct sim ("to leave/set"), whereas the Ketiv spells the synonymous root form sum.
notes.14:11: The Qere reads meharbat ("from multiplying"), whereas the Ketiv has the alternate spelling meharbit.
notes.14:22: The Qere reads "your servant," harmonizing with Joab's direct address to the king, whereas the Ketiv reads "his servant."
notes.14:30: The Qere reads the plural imperative "and set it on fire," matching Absalom's command to his servants, whereas the Ketiv has an alternate verbal spelling.
notes.15:7: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "forty years," preserved faithfully here without harmonizing to ancient versions that read "four years."
notes.15:8: The Masoretic Text notes a Ketiv/Qere variant in the intensifying verbal phrase "indeed brings me back"; the Qere reading is followed here.
notes.15:20: The Qere reads the Hiphil form meaning "should I make you wander," whereas the Ketiv has an alternate spelling with waw.
notes.15:21: The Ketiv includes the particle im ("if") which is omitted in the Qere (Ketiv velo Qere), yielding the direct oath translated here.
notes.15:28: The Qere reads "in the plains of the wilderness," whereas the Ketiv reads "at the fords of the wilderness."
notes.16:2: The Hebrew Qere reads "and the bread," whereas the Ketiv has a scribal form that appears as "and to fight."
notes.16:10: Following the Hebrew Qere ("So let him curse, because the LORD has said to him"); the Ketiv reads "If he curses, and if the LORD has said to him."
notes.16:12: The Hebrew Qere reads "upon my eye," traditionally understood as referring to David's tears; the Ketiv reads "upon my iniquity" or "upon my affliction."
notes.16:18: Following the Hebrew Qere ("his"); the Ketiv is spelled identically to the negative particle ("not").
notes.16:23: The word "a man" is supplied by the Masoretic reading tradition (Qere without Ketiv) to complete the idiom.
notes.17:3: The Masoretic Hebrew is unusually concise here, literally "like the returning of all is the man whom you seek," meaning that dealing with David alone ensures the peaceful return of the entire people.
notes.17:12: The Hebrew Qere adjusts the numeral "one" to the masculine form to agree with the masculine noun "places," whereas the Ketiv uses the feminine form.
notes.17:20: "Brook of water" translates a rare Hebrew phrase occurring only here in the Old Testament, traditionally understood as a small stream or channel of water.
notes.17:25: The Hebrew text here calls Ithra "the Israelite"; the parallel genealogy in First Chronicles calls him "the Ishmaelite."
notes.17:28: The Hebrew repeats the term for roasted or parched produce once after grain and again after beans and lentils, indicating both parched grain and parched pulses or seeds.
notes.18:3: The Masoretic Qere reads the Qal infinitive 'to aid' (la'azor), whereas the Ketiv writes a Hiphil form with the same sense. The Masoretic text also reads 'for now' ('attah) rather than 'for you' ('attah), with the subject 'you' understood from the context of the plea.
notes.18:8: The Masoretic Qere reads the feminine singular participle 'spread out' (nafotset) in grammatical agreement with the singular noun 'battle,' while the Ketiv writes a feminine plural form.
notes.18:12: The Masoretic Qere reads 'even though' (welu) rather than the Ketiv's orthographic variant spelling (welo). The Hebrew text also reads 'whoever you may be' (mi) rather than 'for my sake' (li) as in verse 5.
notes.18:13: The Masoretic Qere reads 'against my own life' (benafshi), whereas the Ketiv reads 'against his life' (benafsho).
notes.18:20: In the Masoretic text, the word 'so' (ken) stands in the consonantal text (Ketiv) but is omitted in the traditional reading (Qere), yielding the causal clause 'because the king's son is dead.'
notes.19:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, 19:1 corresponds to 18:33 in many English Bibles, shifting the numbering of the chapter by one verse.
notes.19:7: Following the Masoretic Qere ("if"); the written Ketiv reads "not."
notes.19:32: Following the Masoretic Qere ("over the Jordan"); the written Ketiv reads "at the Jordan."
notes.19:41: Following the Masoretic Qere ("escorted the king across"); the written Ketiv has a variant verbal form, and Chimham is spelled Chimhan in the Hebrew text of this verse.
notes.20:5: Following the Masoretic Qere ("and he delayed"); the written Ketiv preserves an orthographic variant of the same verb.
notes.20:14: Following the Masoretic Qere ("and they gathered together"); the written Ketiv transposes two consonants of the root.
notes.20:23: Following the Masoretic Qere ("the Cherethites"); the written Ketiv reads "the Carites."
notes.20:25: Following the Masoretic Qere ("Sheva"); the written Ketiv reads "Sheya."
notes.20:26: The Hebrew word kohen ("priest") may also denote a chief royal counselor or minister in David's court (compare 2 Samuel 8:18).
notes.21:6: The Hebrew verb rendered "hang" denotes public ritual execution or exposure before the LORD. The Masoretic Ketiv reads a Niphal form and the Qere reads a Hophal form, both meaning "let them be given."
notes.21:8: The Masoretic Hebrew explicitly reads "Michal" as the mother of Adriel's five sons, whereas 1 Samuel 18:19 names Saul's elder daughter Merab as the wife given to Adriel the Meholathite.
notes.21:16: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere for the name Ishbi-Benob (Ketiv reads "and they dwelt in Nob" or "and Ishbo-Benob"). "The giant" renders Hebrew ha-Raphah (also in verses 18, 20, and 22), an eponym associated with the Rephaim.
notes.21:19: The Masoretic Hebrew states directly that Elhanan struck down Goliath the Gittite, whereas the parallel text in 1 Chronicles 20:5 identifies the Philistine slain by Elhanan as Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.
notes.21:20: The Masoretic Ketiv reads "a man of measures," while the Qere reads madon, meaning "great stature" (or "strife"). In verse 21, "Shimeah" follows the Masoretic Qere (Ketiv: Shimei).
notes.22:8: Qere reads the masculine verb form while Ketiv reads the feminine form agreeing with 'the earth'; both yield the same sense in English.
notes.22:15: Translated from the Qere, which omits the pronominal suffix on the final verb ('and brought confusion'); Ketiv includes the plural suffix ('and routed them').
notes.22:33: Translated from the Qere 'my way'; Ketiv reads 'his way.' The same first-person Qere versus third-person Ketiv variation recurs in verse 34 ('my feet' vs. 'his feet').
notes.22:46: The Masoretic verb here denotes limping or halting, in contrast to the parallel song in Psalm 18, which uses a different verb meaning 'come trembling.'
notes.22:51: Translated from the Qere 'a tower of salvation'; Ketiv reads a participle meaning 'magnifying salvation,' as in the parallel song in Psalm 18.
notes.23:8: Qere reads 'the Eznite' and feminine 'one' agreeing with 'time'; ketiv reads a variant form 'ha-ezno' and masculine 'one.'
notes.23:9: Qere reads 'Dodo' and 'the mighty men' with the definite article; ketiv reads 'Dodai' and 'mighty men.'
notes.23:13: Qere reads 'three' of the thirty chief men; ketiv reads 'thirty.'
notes.23:18: Qere reads 'the three' (matching v. 19); ketiv reads 'the captains' or 'officers.'
notes.23:20: Qere reads 'a valiant man' and 'the lion'; ketiv reads 'a living man' and an alternate spelling of 'the lion.' In v. 21, qere reads 'a man' where ketiv reads 'who.'
notes.23:35: Qere reads 'Hezrai' (ketiv: 'Hezro'). In v. 37, qere reads singular 'armor-bearer' (ketiv: plural 'armor-bearers').
notes.24:13: The Masoretic Hebrew reads 'seven years of famine,' in contrast to 'three years' in 1 Chronicles 21:12.
notes.24:16: Qere reads 'Araunah' here and in v. 18; ketiv preserves alternate consonantal spellings of the Jebusite name.
notes.24:23: The Hebrew 'hammelek' may be understood either as a vocative ('O king') within Araunah's address or in apposition ('Araunah the king').
notes.24:25: The Hebrew verb denotes the LORD answering supplication on behalf of the land, bringing the plague to an end.
